answer: Using a logistic regression model with age as the only predictor, the predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR with treatment in a patient aged 65 is approximately 0.40 (0.395, i.e., ~39.5%). Note: because all 41 patients in the treatment group achieved PR (zero outcome variance, making a treatment-arm-only model unidentifiable), the unpenalized logistic regression was fitted on the pooled sample of all 80 patients, with the binary outcome defined as PR = 1 vs SD/PD = 0 and Age entered as a continuous linear predictor.
